learning_outcomes.text: Acquire basic knowledge of Probability Theory and Mathematical Statistics, with main focus on applications
Become familiar and be able to work with various probabilistic and statistical models
Ability to perform statistical analysis of data
Ability to use statistical features of various mathematical software
Defining basic concepts, theory and mathematical models
Identifying the appropriate models and methods for solving real-life problems
Embedding formal models in applications from various areas

Ability to conform to the requirements of organized and efficient work, to develop a responsible approach towards the academic and scientific fields, in order to make the most of one’s own creative potential, while obeying the rules and principles of professional ethic

Using efficient methods and techniques for learning, information, research and developing capabilities for using knowledge, for adapting to a dynamic society and for communicating in Romanian and in a worldwide spoken language

syllabus_topics: Experiments, events, field of events, operations with events. Axiomatic definition of probability. Poincaré’s formula. Classical definition of probability.
Conditional probability. Independent events. Total probability formula. Classical probabilistic models (Binomial, Hypergeometric, Poisson, Pascal, Geometric).
Random variables and random vectors. Discrete random variables. Probability distribution function. Cumulative distribution function. Properties, examples.
Discrete probability laws (Bernoulli, Binomial, Hypergeometric, Poisson, Negative Binomial, Geometric). Discrete random vectors. Operations with discrete random variables.

Continuous random variables. Probability density function. Continuous probability laws (Uniform, Normal, Gamma, Exponential, Chi-square, Student, Fisher). Independent random variables. Functions of continuous random variables.
Numerical characteristics of random variables. Expectation. Variance and standard deviation. Median. Moments (initial, central, absolute).
Quantiles. Covariance and correlation coefficient. Inequalities (Markov, Chebyshev). Central limit theorem.
Descriptive statistics. Data collection. Graphical display of data. Frequency distribution, histograms, stem-and-leaf plots. Parameters of a statistical distribution. Measures of central tendency.
Measures of variation. Correlation and regression. Linear regression, least squares estimation.

Statistical inference. Sample theory. Samples. Sample functions (sample mean, sample variance, sample moments). Estimation theory, basic notions. Confidence intervals for estimating the population mean and the population variance.
Confidence intervals for comparing two population means and two population variances. Hypothesis testing, basic notions. Rejection region. Type I errors. Significance testing and P-values.
Tests for the parameters of one population Tests for comparing the parameters of two populations. Examples. Robust tests. Summary of hypothesis testing.

Properties of point estimators. Unbiased and minimum variance estimators. Fisher’s information. Absolutely correct estimators. The Rao-Cramer inequality. Efficient estimators. Methods of estimation (method of moments, method of maximum likelihood). Examples.
Type II errors and the power of a test. Most powerful tests and the Neyman-Pearson lemma. Uniformly most powerful tests. Examples.
Euler's Functions. Properties. Counting, Outcomes, Events.
Classical Probability. Rules of Probability. Conditional Probability. Independent Events.
Probabilistic models.
Discrete random variables and discrete random vectors.
Continuous random variables and continuous random vectors.
Numerical characteristics of random variables.
Inequalities. Central Limit Theorem. Point Estimators.
Introduction to Matlab.
Estimating probability by computer simulations.
Discrete random variables. PDF and CDF.
Continuous random variables. PDF, CDF and Inverse CDF.
Descriptive Statistics. Statistical measures. Correlation and regression.
Confidence intervals and tests for the mean and variance.
Confidence intervals and tests for the difference of means and ratio of variances.

assessment_methods.method: Seminar activities (participation, documentation, individual presentation, solving bonus problems)
Lab activities (participation, individual presentation of solutions)

assessment_rules: A minimum grade of 5 (on a scale of 1 to 10) is required on each of the three evaluation activities: written test, seminar evaluation, and lab evaluation.
